title: How to support a goal system in sepo?
body:
Right now we have a clear definition of how small goals should be specified with issues and PRs. But how to track bigger objectives -- the purposes of the whole repository? And can it be updated accordingly? 

@sepo-agent /answer

nodes.body:
Yes. I’d support this as a separate **repo-goals layer**, above issues/PRs and above current project-management labels.

Current pieces already exist:

- `agent/memory` has `PROJECT.md` for slow-changing project context, including goals/open questions: [memory.md#L9-L16](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L9-L16)
- repo-scoped workflows already use `target_kind=repository`, so a goals pass does not need to attach to one issue/PR: [key-concepts.md#L70-L80](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/key-concepts.md#L70-L80)
- `agent-project-manager.yml` already inspects open issues/PRs and emits a structured plan, but today it is backlog triage, not repository purpose tracking: [supported-workflows.md#L145-L160](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md#L145-L160)
- the current project-manager is still label-plan oriented: [project-manager.md#L9-L51](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/project-manager.md#L9-L51), [project-management-labels.ts#L29-L39](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/project-management-labels.ts#L29-L39)

Recommended design:

- Keep **issues/PRs** as small executable tasks.
- Keep **GitHub Project / project-manager** as prioritization and planning UI.
- Add **Goals** as repo-level strategic objectives: “why this repo exists and what it is trying to become.”
- Store canonical goals in a human-reviewable artifact, probably `GOALS.md` or `.agent/goals/goals.yml` on the default branch.
- Mirror/summarize active goals into `agent/memory/PROJECT.md` so normal Sepo runs can use them as context.
- Do not let the agent silently rewrite canonical goals during ordinary `/answer`, `/implement`, or `/orchestrate` runs. Goal changes should be proposed through PRs or an explicit privileged route.

A minimal goal record could be:

```yaml
id: hosted-onboarding
title: Make hosted Sepo onboarding reliable
status: active
horizon: near-term
why: Reduce setup friction for new repositories.
success_criteria:
  - Hosted App install flow works end-to-end.
  - Onboarding setup check gives actionable status.
linked_items:
  issues: [123, 124]
  prs: []
updated_at: 2026-05-16
```

Implementation plan:

1. Add a canonical goals file, either `GOALS.md` for readability or `.agent/goals/goals.yml` for automation.
2. Add docs explaining the hierarchy: goals -> projects/roadmap -> issues/PRs.
3. Add a `goal` or `goals` helper module that parses and validates the goals file.
4. Update prompts so `/answer`, `/implement`, `/review`, `/orchestrate`, and project-manager runs read active goals as context.
5. Add a scheduled or manual “goal review” workflow that compares open issues/PRs against goals and reports drift.
6. Let that workflow propose updates, but apply canonical goal changes only through PRs.
7. Later, add GitHub Project sync: Project fields can link items to goal IDs, while goals remain the strategic source of truth.

So the answer is: **yes, Sepo should have a goal system, but it should not be just bigger issues.** It should be a repo-scoped, reviewable goals document plus agent memory summaries and project-manager alignment checks.

I’d start with the simplest task: add the goals schema/docs and wire active goals into project-manager context. Once that is accepted, we can add the scheduled goal-review workflow.
@sepo-agent /answer this seems to be  the right starting point; but also reflect how this might interact with #223 #173 #160 ; also the recently added self-approval and self-merge functions?

Yes, I think this is the right starting point, but the goal system should be treated as a **coordination layer**, not just another task type.

I’d frame the stack like this:

```text
Goals = why / success criteria / strategic direction
Project planning = what is active, prioritized, or scheduled
Issues/PRs = executable units
Orchestrator = moves executable units forward
Self-approval/self-merge = closes trusted PR loops
Experiments = measured trial loops under a goal
Self-improvement = proposes changes to Sepo itself under goals
```

How it interacts with the referenced threads:

- **#223 / auto-research**: a goal gives the research loop its durable objective, but it should not store trial logs. For example, a goal can say “improve long-running experiment support,” while `ExperimentSpec` / `ExperimentRun` records handle metrics, trial IDs, artifact URIs, best result, and parallel lanes. This matches the earlier conclusion in #223: the missing abstraction is structured experiment state, not just another orchestrator transition.

- **#173 / orchestrator reflection**: goals are exactly the context the reflection gate should use. When an orchestrated chain starts becoming patchy or expanding scope, the planner should compare the current PR against the original issue, active goal, success criteria, and anti-goals. If the PR no longer advances the goal cleanly, it should stop, split, supersede, or ask a human instead of continuing to `fix-pr`.

- **#160 / self-improvement**: the proposed daily self-improvement workflow should choose ideas by looking for gaps against active goals plus recent failures. External repo scanning can be an inspiration lane, but the proposal should still answer: “which active Sepo goal does this advance?” If none, it should not create work automatically.

- **Self-approval/self-merge**: these should remain safety gates, not goal-selection mechanisms. The current flow already says `review: SHIP -> agent-self-approve -> agent-self-merge` only when enabled, and runtime policy validates the transitions: [agent-orchestrator.md#L20-L39](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L20-L39). A goal system can add context to self-approval, but it should not weaken the deterministic checks. Self-approval still requires trusted current-head review provenance and distinct actor checks in code, and self-merge still requires current-head self-approval, checks, and mergeability.

Concretely, I’d add goals as a human-reviewable source of truth, probably `GOALS.md` or `.agent/goals/goals.yml`, then mirror a short active-goals summary into `agent/memory/PROJECT.md`. Memory already has a slot for slow-changing project goals: [memory.md#L9-L16](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L9-L16), but canonical goal changes should go through PRs, not silent memory edits.

A minimal goal object should include:

```yaml
id: experiment-runtime
title: Support structured computational experiment loops
status: active
success_criteria:
  - Experiment specs can define metric, budget, backend, and artifacts.
  - Completed trials produce deterministic result records.
  - Improved code candidates can flow through review/self-approval/self-merge.
links:
  discussions: [223]
  issues: []
```

Recommended first implementation slice:

1. Add goals schema/docs.
2. Add one canonical goals file with initial goals.
3. Teach project-manager/orchestrator prompts to read active goals.
4. Add a reflection field like `goal_alignment: aligned | drift | unclear`.
5. Do **not** auto-update goals yet; propose goal changes by PR.

After that, the next slices are: goal-aware orchestrator reflection for #173, goal-linked experiment specs for #223, and goal-constrained self-improvement proposals for #160.

Another way is to use a discussion thread to manage goals? 

@sepo-agent /answer

Yes. A Discussion thread is probably the best **human-facing surface** for goals.

I would not make the raw discussion prose the only source of truth, though. The clean model is:

```text
Discussion thread = collaborative goal notebook
Structured snapshot = machine-readable current goals
Memory PROJECT.md = short agent-facing summary
Issues/PRs = execution units linked back to goals
```

Why Discussions fit well:

- Sepo already supports discussion triggers and discussion comments: [supported-workflows.md#L198-L203](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md#L198-L203)
- It can post normal comments or threaded replies to discussions: [respond.ts#L56-L64](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/respond.ts#L56-L64)
- It already has transcript fetching for full discussion context, including replies: [discussion-transcript.ts#L207-L276](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/discussion-transcript.ts#L207-L276)
- Memory already has `PROJECT.md` for slow-changing goals/constraints/open questions: [memory.md#L9-L16](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L9-L16)

Suggested design:

- Create one pinned discussion, e.g. **Repository Goals**.
- The discussion body contains the current goal index.
- Each top-level comment represents one goal.
- Replies under that comment record decisions, progress, objections, and revisions.
- Sepo periodically or manually summarizes the accepted state into a structured snapshot.

Example discussion shape:

```md
## Active Goals

<!-- sepo-goals-index -->

- `hosted-onboarding`: Make hosted Sepo onboarding reliable
- `experiment-runtime`: Support structured computational experiment loops
- `goal-system`: Add repo-level goal tracking
```

Example goal comment:

```md
<!-- sepo-goal id:experiment-runtime status:active -->

## Support Structured Computational Experiment Loops

Why:
Sepo needs a first-class experiment lifecycle for auto-research style work.

Success criteria:
- Experiment specs define metric, budget, backend, and artifacts.
- Completed runs produce deterministic result records.
- Improved code candidates can flow through review/self-approval/self-merge.

Links:
- Discussion: #223
```

The important guardrail: **discussion updates should be easy, but activation should be explicit**. For example:

- Anyone allowed by policy can discuss goals.
- Sepo can summarize proposed goal changes.
- Only an explicit command like `/goals apply` or `/setup apply` should update the structured snapshot.
- The structured snapshot then feeds project-manager, orchestrator reflection, self-improvement, and self-approval context.

First implementation slice I’d recommend:

1. Add docs for the “Goals Discussion” convention.
2. Add a deterministic parser for `<!-- sepo-goal ... -->` blocks.
3. Add a manual `agent-goals-sync.yml` workflow that reads the configured discussion and produces a validated goals summary.
4. Write the short summary into `agent/memory/PROJECT.md`.
5. Later, add PR-backed updates to a canonical `.agent/goals/goals.yml`.

So yes: use a Discussion thread to manage goals, but pair it with a structured snapshot so agents do not have to infer the repository’s purpose from an ever-growing conversation every time.

@sepo-agent /answer


> Suggested design:
> Create one pinned discussion, e.g. Repository Goals.

This should be a category for discussions; for each post it can denote a specific goal. we can talk about how the goal is achieved and optimized in the process. 

If needed, we can use agent/goal branch to track? actually not really sure if at this stage we need that goal chain of history

Yes, I agree with that revision: **“Goals” should be a Discussion category**, not one pinned mega-thread.

That gives a cleaner object model:

```text
Discussion category: Goals
Each discussion: one goal
Discussion body: current goal definition
Comments/replies: progress, reflection, optimization, decisions
Issues/PRs: concrete work linked from the goal
Memory PROJECT.md: short active-goals summary for agents
```

This fits Sepo’s current primitives. Discussions are already first-class trigger/response surfaces, and Sepo can fetch full discussion transcripts including replies: [discussion-transcript.ts#L207-L292](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/discussion-transcript.ts#L207-L292). Memory already has `PROJECT.md` for slow-changing goals and constraints: [memory.md#L9-L18](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L9-L18).

I would **not add an `agent/goal` branch yet**. At this stage, the Discussion history is probably enough:

- the goal body is the current state;
- comments capture reasoning and process;
- replies capture local threads;
- linked issues/PRs show execution;
- Sepo can periodically summarize active goals into `agent/memory/PROJECT.md`.

A separate `agent/goal` or `agent/goals` branch becomes useful later only if we need machine-readable snapshots with versioned diffs, conflict control, or automation that must not depend on discussion prose.

Suggested v0 convention:

```md
# Goal: Support structured computational experiments

Status: active
Horizon: mid-term

Why:
Sepo should support iterative experiment loops, not only code feature loops.

Success criteria:
- Experiment specs can define metrics, budgets, and compute backends.
- Results are recorded deterministically.
- Improved candidates can flow through review/self-approval/self-merge.

Linked work:
- Discussions: #223
- Issues:
- PRs:

Current strategy:
Start with structured experiment state and local runner support.
```

Then Sepo can post/update comments like:

```md
## Goal Progress Update

- New evidence:
- Completed work:
- Current blockers:
- Suggested next issue:
- Goal status change: none / active / blocked / done
```

Implementation order I’d suggest:

1. Add docs for a `Goals` discussion category and goal discussion template.
2. Add a lightweight goal-summary workflow that reads active goal discussions and updates `PROJECT.md`.
3. Teach project-manager/orchestrator/self-improvement prompts to read the active-goals summary.
4. Later, add structured hidden markers or YAML blocks if the discussion category starts driving automation.
5. Only add an `agent/goals` branch if discussion + memory summary becomes too loose.

So the right starting point is: **Goals category + one discussion per goal + memory summary**, with no separate goal branch yet.

@sepo-agent /answer 

ok thinking a bit more about it: 
1. we should not use discussion category; rather we just create issues with goal (labels or some form of text represnetation) 
2. issue provides a way for us to create sub issues -> that manages concrete tasks 
3. sub-issue hierarchy provides us ways to break down a goal into smaller subgoals and implement it. we can also reuse our orchestrate infrastructure for that.

I agree. For Sepo’s current architecture, **goal-as-issue** is probably better than goal-as-discussion.

Reason: `/orchestrate` already works on issues, and the existing meta-orchestrator can create/reuse/adopt child issues through `delegate_issue`: [agent-orchestrator.md#L83-L110](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L83-L110). The docs also say parent/child state is intentionally kept in GitHub issue metadata, not session state: [agent-orchestrator.md#L119-L130](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L119-L130). That lines up almost exactly with your goal/subgoal/task model.

I’d revise the model to:

```text
Goal issue = strategic objective
Sub-issues = subgoals or workstreams
Leaf issues = concrete implementable tasks
PRs = execution artifacts
Parent goal comments = progress, reflection, replanning
PROJECT.md = short cached summary for future agent context
```

Minimal representation:

- Add one label: `goal`
- Optional status labels later: `goal/active`, `goal/paused`, `goal/done`
- Prefer structured issue body over many labels.

Example goal issue body:

```md
## Goal

Support structured computational experiment loops in Sepo.

## Why

Sepo should support iterative measured experiments, not only code-feature loops.

## Success Criteria

- Experiment specs define metric, budget, backend, and artifacts.
- Runs produce deterministic result records.
- Improved candidates can flow through review/self-approval/self-merge.

## Current Strategy

Start with structured experiment state and local-runner support.

## Subgoals

- [ ] Experiment spec schema
- [ ] Result ledger
- [ ] Local adapter
- [ ] Slurm adapter
- [ ] Orchestrator integration

<!-- sepo-goal v1 status:active horizon:mid-term -->
```

Then `@sepo-agent /orchestrate` on the goal issue can either:

- create/adopt a sub-issue for the next subgoal;
- stack child PRs when sequential work depends on prior PRs;
- stop and ask for human direction when the next subgoal is unclear.

That reuses the existing machinery instead of creating a separate goal system from scratch. The current orchestrator prompt already says issue-level orchestration can delegate when separate child issues materially help: [agent-orchestrator.md#L81-L89](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L81-L89).

On `agent/goal`: I would **not add that branch yet**. The issue hierarchy already gives us the goal chain of history:

- issue body = current goal definition;
- comments = decisions and progress;
- sub-issues = decomposition;
- PRs = implementation trail;
- closed sub-issues = completed subgoals.

A separate `agent/goal` branch becomes useful only if we later need deterministic snapshots, goal diffing, or machine-readable state beyond what issue bodies/comments can safely provide. For now, `agent/memory/PROJECT.md` can hold only a short summary of active goals, since memory already has a place for slow-changing goals/constraints: [memory.md#L9-L18](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L9-L18).

So the new starting point should be:

1. Add a `goal` issue label.
2. Add a goal issue template.
3. Document goal issue conventions.
4. Update orchestrator guidance to treat `goal` issues as meta-orchestration parents.
5. Add a lightweight goal-summary pass that syncs active goal summaries into `PROJECT.md`.

That is simpler and better aligned with Sepo than a Discussion category or a new branch.
